inspiration.observed_pattern: Minimized reproduction of the parent-minus-children pattern from self_join_null_delta: a two-row tree where the root's direct child is the only non-NULL aggregate, so the parent subtraction is a number while the leaf subtraction stays NULL. Before the fix, the self-join matched no rows at all, so every subtraction was NULL.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Same translation as self_join_null_delta: plan operations become ledger entries, NVL stays out of this minimal case, and the raw nullable subtraction is projected so an empty aggregate is observable.

fixture_notes: Row 2 is the only child of row 1; row 1 must report 10 minus 3, row 2 must report NULL, not 7, because a self-join must match parent id against child parent_id, not the reverse.
determinism_notes: Single read-only statement; ORDER BY the unique primary key.
setup: CREATE TABLE entries (id INT PRIMARY KEY, parent_id INT, amount INT)

steps.sql: SELECT p.id, p.amount - SUM(c.amount) AS unexplained FROM entries p LEFT JOIN entries c ON c.parent_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.amount ORDER BY p.id
